title: I2C Bus Explorer
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: An I2C transaction rendered as a schematic, a logic-analyser waveform and a simulated i2cdetect grid from one shared state machine, with five injectable faults matching the chapter's troubleshooting list.

learningObjectives: Examine an I2C transaction and explain how addressing lets many devices share two wires.
Read an i2cdetect grid and say what it rules in and out.
Diagnose common bus faults from their symptoms.
Explain why two devices may not share an address on one bus.
prerequisites: Chapter 3: pull-up resistors and the GPIO header
Chapter 12: I2C, device addresses and i2cdetect

keyQuestions: How can three devices share two wires without interfering?
What does an empty i2cdetect grid tell you, and what does it not tell you?
Which fault looks most like a bug in your code, and why?
What happens on the wire when two devices answer at once?
commonMisconceptions: Each sensor needs its own pair of wires.
An empty i2cdetect grid means the code is wrong.
Two identical sensors can always be used on one bus.
The controller can tell how many devices acknowledged.
assessmentOpportunities: Converts the seven broadcast address bits to hex by hand and checks against the panel.
Identifies an injected fault from the grid and waveform alone.
Explains why breakout boards provide an address-select pin.
